edit.description: the history append preserves the lines it read rather than re-serializing the records its own structural check accepted
the preserved row, beside the tick-verdict artifact block's own history cases

summary: The history append rewrites the log from decoded records, so every row a field added to the structural check declines is deleted on the next tick — the spec states never cleared

per.section: The tick verdict — one facts artifact

acceptance: a row the structural check declines survives the next tick's append, so a field added to the verdict shape costs the log nothing and `<flumeDir>/tick-verdicts.jsonl` is the history the spec states, with the rolling bound and what `readTickVerdicts` hands a chain unchanged
tests: the verdict history append keeps a record the structural check declines
notes: Measured this tick over a two-row log: the pre-`timings` row is dropped by the read (`isTickVerdict`, `src/tickVerdict.ts:917`; the new arm `:928`) and the rewrite (`:1003`) puts back only what the read returned. Every field ever added did the same, silently. `MAX_TICK_VERDICTS` then bounds lines as well as records.
